## 1 A common reference and compatible smoothing

Closing E in the compact state space leaves all three quantities unchanged. The continuous entropy graph has compact convex hull in real dimension at most d². Consequently a finite prior attains C(E); let σ be its mean. For every ρ∈E one has D(ρ||σ)≤C(E). Here is a proof covering singular supports: mix ρ at mass t into the maximizing prior, so σ_t=(1−t)σ+tρ. The relative-entropy decomposition of the new Holevo quantity gives

χ_t=(1−t)C(E)+(1−t)D(σ||σ_t)+tD(ρ||σ_t)≤C(E).

Thus D(ρ||σ_t)≤C(E); lower semicontinuity as t↓0 yields the claim and support containment. Since σ is a finite convex combination of promised states, adjoining it leaves capacity and any broadcaster's uniform error bound unchanged. Restricting to P=suppσ is physically legitimate using the CPTP output map X↦PXP+Tr[(I−P)X]σ; later reconstruction channels extend by input pinching and fixed preparation. We may henceforth assume σ faithful.

Fix a smoothing tolerance 0<δ<1/2, and set

η=δ²/8, M=(1−η)⁻¹exp[(C+ln2)/η], λ=η/M.

The quantum substate theorem supplies, for every ρ∈E, a state τ₀≤Mσ with squared fidelity at least 1−η. The factor follows from observational relative divergence in bits being at most relative entropy in bits plus one; conversion to nats gives the displayed M. This is an established imported theorem, not a new assertion here.

On the compact convex set K_σ={0≤τ≤Mσ, Trτ≤1}, minimize

J_(ρ,σ)(τ)=−F_root(ρ,τ)+λQ_σ(τ),
Q_σ(X)=||σ^(−1/4)Xσ^(−1/4)||₂².

Call the unique minimizer G(ρ,σ). Fidelity concavity and positive-definite quadratic curvature yield the exact gap

J(v)−J(G)≥λQ_σ(v−G)≥λ||v−G||₁².

The last inequality is Schatten Hölder duality and Trσ=1. On K_σ, Q_σ(τ)≤MTrτ≤M, so comparison with τ₀ gives F_root(ρ,G)≥1−2η. Hence t=TrG≥(1−2η)²>1/2, and the state ρhat=G/t satisfies ρhat≤2Mσ and T(ρhat,ρ)≤δ. At ρ=σ the scalar bound J(v)≥−sqrt(Trv)+λ(Trv)², minimized at trace one, shows by uniqueness that G(σ,σ)=σ. Thus σ is included exactly in the smoothed family.

The essential feature is compatibility with a channel, not merely pointwise approximation. For any CPTP T with d_ρ=||Tρ−ρ||₁ and d_σ=||Tσ−σ||₁, define

ξ=sqrt(d_ρ)+(sqrt(M)+2λM²)sqrt(d_σ)+(M/2)d_σ.

Then the same optimizer obeys

||T G(ρ,σ)−G(ρ,σ)||₁
≤(1+sqrt2)sqrt(ξ/λ)+2M sqrt(d_σ)+M d_σ.                 (A)

# Independent audit: uniform capacity to a fixed sandwich

Date: 2026-10-09. Audited source: `sources/d-b4ddaa96b233287d.txt` (the October 7 compatible-smoothing audit). This is a new mathematical reconstruction of that reduction, not an audit of the separate fixed-sandwich theorem or a priority claim.

## Verdict

**The reduction is valid for arbitrary nonempty families of states in finite-dimensional spaces, allowing dimension and family size to grow along a sequence. No fatal gap found.** Its hypotheses are genuinely uniform: Holevo capacity is the supremum over all finite priors, broadcast error is a supremum over promised states and both marginals, and EB error is the infimum over one common channel of a supremum over promised states. A bound on Holevo information for one prescribed prior cannot replace capacity.

The conclusion is an equivalence of two sequence implications, conditional on the fixed-sandwich gate. This audit does not prove that gate. Necessary qualifications are: close each family before taking a capacity-maximizing prior; compress channels by an actual CPTP retraction, not by output projection alone; retain the center as a promised smoothed state; fix smoothing accuracy before taking the sequence limit. These qualifications already appear in the audited source.

A cleaner common-center proof below avoids differentiating entropy at singular states. An explicit modulus makes dimension independence and the order of quantifiers transparent.

## 1. Exact definitions and common center

Write T(rho,tau)=||rho-tau||_1/2. For an experiment E on H, set

- C(E)=sup_p [S(sum_i p_i rho_i)-sum_i p_i S(rho_i)], over all finite priors on E, with natural logarithms;
- b_2(E)=inf_B sup_{rho in E} max_{j=1,2} T(B_j(rho),rho), where one channel B:H→H⊗H supplies both marginals;
- e(E)=inf_{Lambda EB} sup_{rho in E} T(Lambda(rho),rho).

Replacing E by its closure preserves these three quantities in fixed finite dimension. For capacity this follows from entropy continuity and approximation of every finite collection of closure points. For the other two quantities it follows channel by channel from continuity.

# Independent audit: two-state broadcasting implies a small fidelity-affinity gap

## Verdict

The imported N46 two-state bridge is valid. Its decisive finite-dimensional proof can be reconstructed directly. In particular, it does not require the qualitative ultraproduct, finite-mixture, compact-experiment, or almost-commuting arguments elsewhere in N46.

Let T(rho,sigma) = (1/2)||rho-sigma||_1. Suppose a single CPTP channel B sends the input system to two copies of that system, with marginal channels T_0,T_1, and

max_{x=0,1; a=0,1} T(T_a(rho_x),rho_x) <= b.

Then for every integer L >= 0 there is a single EB channel E_L such that

max_x T(E_L(rho_x),rho_x) <= eta_L(b),
eta_L(b) = L b + sqrt(ln(2)/(2*2^L)).

Consequently, with root fidelity F(rho,sigma) = ||sqrt(rho)sqrt(sigma)||_1 and affinity A(rho,sigma) = Tr(sqrt(rho)sqrt(sigma)),

Delta(rho_0,rho_1) = F(rho_0,rho_1)-A(rho_0,rho_1)
 <= min(1, inf_{L>=0 integer} 2 sqrt(2 eta_L(b))).

This is a dimension-free modulus v(b) tending to zero and of order O(sqrt(b log(1/b))). No common reference, support, faithfulness, domination, state entropy, reversibility, or dimension bound is needed for this pair implication. The same broadcaster must work on both states and both receivers.
